abstract: Designing a protein to resist tension requires identifying the contacts that bear the load. We developed ProFORGE to track residues as a scaffold changes length and to select designs by steered molecular dynamics. Starting with the 56-residue GB1 domain, we generated 14,542 candidates using protein language models for scaffold expansion and fixed-backbone design for sequence refinement. Of 182 sequences that passed the initial screen in the final round, 19 also met the AlphaFold 3 confidence threshold. The number of backbone hydrogen bonds between the terminal strands correlated with mean peak force at both simulated pulling speeds (Spearman \ensuremath{\rho} = 0.83--0.85). Two 98-residue designs shared less than 10\% global sequence identity with wild-type GB1. In single-molecule magnetic-tweezers measurements, their most probable unfolding forces were 117.9 and 132.1~pN, or 5.5 and 5.8 times those of the wild-type domains measured on the same tethers.
